implementation_notes: AMQP-CPP gives an event-driven AMQP 0-9-1 client: AMQP::Channel::publish() for the outbound direction and AMQP::Channel::consume() with a handler object for the inbound one, driven by an event-loop handler (libev, libuv or Asio). The adapter is a thin class that implements the application's interface, serializes application data into the payload and invokes application callbacks from the consume handler, so the classic adapter class is retained - the library only provides the protocol client. Choose this variant when a broker is available and the application must not see AMQP types.
pitfalls: AMQP-CPP is asynchronous: publishes issued after a channel error are silently discarded, and calls from another thread must be dispatched onto the loop, not made directly.
Handlers and response objects handed to consume()/publish() must outlive the event-loop iteration that uses them; temporaries destroyed too early are a classic use-after-free.

variants.name: cppzmq brokerless socket adapter
variants.idiom_name: zmq::socket_t push/pull and pub/sub with multipart frames
variants.implementation_notes: For brokerless messaging, cppzmq (header-only libzmq binding) wraps message-oriented sockets: the adapter owns a zmq::socket_t, connects it to a known endpoint and maps application calls to multipart frames sent with send_multipart, while the inbound side receives into a message and dispatches to the application. Choose it when no broker may be deployed or when the application wants its own routing convention (PUSH/PULL for work distribution, PUB/SUB for events); unlike AMQP there is no server-side queueing, so the adapter owns buffering and availability policy.
pitfalls: A PUSH socket queues nothing durable: with no connected peer it blocks (or returns EAGAIN with ZMQ_DONTWAIT), so the adapter must define what happens when the consumer is absent.
libzmq sockets are not thread-safe and a context must outlive all of them; sharing one socket across threads or terminating the context early corrupts the connection.
